rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Satan has no authority to redirect people as he wishes; his role is limited to inviting them to vice.
rows.anchor: The verse says that he does not have any such authority. The only option he has is to invite people to vice

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Satan's respite tests whether people remain faithful despite his lures or succumb to doubts and are led astray.
rows.anchor: this respite has been given to him so that God can test people as to who among them has a faith strong enough

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A verb meaning that God gave Satan respite is understood before “that We may know”; Islahi notes similar ellipses in earlier sūras.
rows.anchor: is suppressed before َمَلْعَنِل and examples of such oppression can be seen in earlier sūrahs.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God remains guardian over all affairs after setting people and Satan to the test, so Satan cannot overstep his bounds and human invocations are not left unanswered.
rows.anchor: He has not detached Himself from their affairs; in fact, He is looking after everything.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who fulfill their duty receive God's help in this world and reward for their deeds; they should not give up from despair of Satan's influence, since God has not handed the world to him.
rows.anchor: If a person fulfills His obligation to the best of his ability God will help in this world and will also richly reward all his deeds.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because mercy and punishment belong to God, the following passage challenges idolaters to prove their deities' partnership; if their claim rests only on arrogance, the Prophet should leave their case to God, the best judge.
rows.anchor: It is evident from the previous verses that mercy and punishment are in the hands of God.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening passage substantiates the promise of resurrection made earlier in verse 5.
rows.anchor: In the succeeding verses, first the promise certain to be fulfilled mentioned in verse 5 earlier is substantiated.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those seeking nearness to God and success should abandon the false deities' path and adopt the right way of faith and righteous deeds.
rows.anchor: should leave aside procuring the nearness of false deities and adopt the right way.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Faith rises to God, while righteous deeds support and elevate it; together they constitute the sole right path.
rows.anchor: Faith is something which ascends to God, and righteous deeds lend support to it and elevates it. This is the only right way.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who abandon the right way and work to turn others from it will eventually see their schemes shattered.
rows.anchor: striving day and night to make people leave the right way will one day find their conspiracies shattered.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God alone controls wealth, children, and changes in lifespan; the universe's harmony confirms that no angel, jinn, or alleged deity has authority.
rows.anchor: increase in wealth and children and increase or decrease in age and other similar things rest with God

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The call benefits people, who need God while He needs nothing from them; acceptance brings success in both worlds and rejection brings ruin.
rows.anchor: God does not need them; on the contrary, they need God.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This passage reassures the Prophet by identifying the kinds of people who will accept the call and those who will be deprived of it.
rows.anchor: an assurance is sounded to the Prophet (sws) by informing him what type of people will accept this call

none: English translation of verses only; no separate commentary point.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The revived dead land is a familiar natural proof that resurrection is possible: winds gather clouds, rain revives barren ground, and the dead will rise similarly on Judgement Day.
rows.anchor: It is common observation that a land is totally dry and desolate

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The world itself serves as a lesson in Qur'anic teaching, and a thoughtful person can find evidence around him for every Qur'anic claim.
rows.anchor: this world by its very existence is the best teaching place of what the Qur’ān teaches.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The shift from past to indefinite to first-person verbs narrates an event, presents an ongoing scene, and conveys affection, respectively.
rows.anchor: the past tense only comes to narrate an incident, indefinite tense portrays an existing situation and the first person verbs signify affection.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All honour belongs to God; anyone honoured receives it through relationship with God and His bestowal.
rows.anchor: will receive honour will receive it because of their relationship with God and because of His endowment.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pure word that rises to God is faith; righteous deeds support and strengthen it, and no other path brings God's nearness.
rows.anchor: what rises to God from human beings is the word of faith. No other thing can become a source of acquiring His nearness.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Faith is like a luxuriant grapevine that needs support: righteous deeds nourish it to fruitfulness, while faith without deeds withers.
rows.anchor: the word of faith is like a grape vine which in itself is luxuriant

rows.speaker: عبدالله بن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās understands “the pure word” as the word of faith, with the adjacent mention of righteous deeds supporting that reading.
rows.anchor: In the opinion of ‘Abdullāh ibn ‘Abbās (rta),

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The adjective ṭayyib describes the faith-word's lushness and luxuriance.
rows.anchor: refers to lushness and luxuriance of the word.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the philosophy of religion, the word of faith is the foundation of knowledge and wisdom and the key to their treasures.
rows.anchor: with regard to the philosophy of religion it is this word which is the foundation of all knowledge and wisdom.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Faith and righteous deeds require one another: deeds lack a basis without faith, and faith is lifeless without deeds.
rows.anchor: faith and righteous deeds necessitate one another. Just as righteous deeds have no basis without faith

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Islahi directs readers to his discussion of the faith-and-deeds image at 14:24–26 in Sūrah Ibrāhīm.
rows.anchor: readers are advised to look up what I have written while explaining verses 24-26 of Sūrah Ibrāhīm.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Idolaters think angel deities will secure success and honour before God, but the true means of nearness is faith supported by righteous deeds.
rows.anchor: The Idolaters are explained that they think that their angel deities will earn success and honour for them before God

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an illustrates the idolaters' belief that they worship deities to bring them nearer to God with the cited parallel at 39:3.
rows.anchor: We worship them only so that they may bring us nearer to God.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cited verse describes idolaters setting up deities as a source of honour for themselves, paralleling their false hope of status through them.
rows.anchor: And they have set up other deities besides God so that they can become a source of honour for them.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Islahi refutes the idolaters' belief that their deities can procure honour and tells them to seek it through faith and righteous deeds.
rows.anchor: In the verse under discussion, it is this false notion of theirs which is refuted.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who plot to protect their pride and harm God's religion and messenger will gain no honour; their schemes invite grievous doom.
rows.anchor: people who instead of facing this reality plot evil schemes to protect their pride and to harm God’s religion and His messenger

rows.speaker: al-Zamakhsharī
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī takes the accusative word al-sayyiʾāt as an adjective for an elided verbal noun; Islahi prefers this construction, which is exemplified at 35:43.
rows.anchor:
In the opinion of al-
Zamakhsharī,178 this word is an adjective of a suppressed verbal noun

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repeating the subject adds emphasis: the evil schemes will harm their own authors and become their means of destruction, rather than harming others.
rows.anchor: The repetition of the inchoative (mubtadā’) in the sentence has incorporated a stress in it

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At 35:43, the Qur'an further explains that evil plotting recoils on its authors; truth benefits all, so opposing it brings self-harm.
rows.anchor: Further ahead, more light is shed on this subject by the words

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's knowledge and command govern increases or decreases in age and number of children; idols have no role, so people should turn to God.
rows.anchor: any increase or decrease in age or number of children is in the knowledge of God and takes place with His directive.
